newsitem.title: UK: High oestrogen linked to breast cancer - doctors.
newsitem.headline: High oestrogen linked to breast cancer - doctors.

text.p: Post-menopausal women with high levels of naturally-occuring oestrogen in their blood may have an increased risk of developing breast cancer, British researchers said on Monday.

The researchers from the Imperial Cancer Research Fund (ICRF) said they took blood samples from 2,500 post-menopausal women between 1977 and 1990 and tested the levels of oestradiol, the natural form of oestrogen.

An average of eight years later, 61 of these woman had developed breast cancer. The researchers took further blood samples from the women who developed cancer and compared them with women who had not.

"The women with high levels of oestradiol were found to be up to five times more likely to subsequently develop breast cancer than women with low levels," said Hollie Thomas of the ICRF, in a statement.
"This suggests that high levels of oestradiol are strongly related to breast cancer risk in post-menopausal women."
Thomas said she was sure the high oestradiol levels were present before the cancers developed.

The ICRF said it was now investigating what factors influence the level of oestradiol in the blood. The only well-established factor at present is obesity, which raises oestradiol in women who have passed the menopause.
